review_notes: Verified against the exact vulnerable source extracted from n132/arvo:17069-vul (bitreader.c, stream_decoder.c at commit 6d0e222a).

source bitreader.c:196 `if(!br->read_callback(target, &bytes, br->client_data))` confirmed; this is the input-load point where untrusted stream bytes are materialized into br->buffer (target = br->buffer + br->words). It is project code, not the fuzz-harness wrapper, and it is the fill point of the exact array that is over-read at the sink, so it is a valid source for this heap-buffer-overflow-READ. tainted_value_origin is correctly split out to the vulnerability-relevant field (rice_parameter).

sink/root_cause bitreader.c:867 `b = br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits;` confirmed and matches the ASan crash (bitreader.c:867:8, READ 4, 0 bytes right of the 8192-byte region). The enclosing process_tail do/while at line 868 `} while(cwords >= words && val < end);` confirmed; the read at 867 has no `cwords < br->capacity` guard, so once the residual coding advances cwords to br->capacity (2048 words) the access leaves the buffer. This is exactly the condition the fix repairs: line 867 becomes `b = cwords < br->capacity ? br->buffer[cwords] << br->consumed_bits : 0;` (patch hunk @@ -864,7 +869,7 @@). root_cause is faithful to both source semantics and patch.diff.

stream_decoder.c:2702 (read_residual_partitioned_rice_ dispatch), 2767 (rice_parameter read), and 2773 (FLAC__bitreader_read_rice_signed_block call) all confirmed and consistent with the ASan crash stack (frames #1 stream_decoder.c:2773, #2 stream_decoder.c:2702). fine_trace steps 6 (bitreader.c:843 read_unary_unsigned) and 7 (bitreader.c:864 cwords = br->consumed_words) confirmed.

fine_trace is a genuine data/control-flow trace (source -> words bound -> LPC dispatch -> rice_parameter -> block-decoder dispatch -> unary consume -> cwords materialization -> loop-reentry guard -> missing capacity check -> sink), not a call stack; adjacent-step dependencies are real and the missing `cwords < br->capacity` check is correctly modeled as the control edge at the root_cause/sink.

Minor judgement note (not a defect): reachability_checkpoints.parser_admitted is set to the residual-parse entry (stream_decoder.c:2767), the same line as tainted_value_origin, rather than to an earlier frame-sync / frame-header acceptance point. It is still a valid on-path admission point earlier than the sink, but a stricter format-acceptance checkpoint (frame header validation) would make parser_admitted more clearly distinct from the tainted origin.
No bootstrap wording (first-pass / selected as / requires review) present in final GT fields.
